test_cases.Test Description: Validates default reset values and masked write/read behavior across GPIO per-pin control, group interrupt, IO control, and data registers using AHB register accesses.
test_cases.Remarks: VRRW locations are intentionally skipped during write/read. During default-value reads, input value may self-bias high unless forced low, affecting expected match.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: test starts and first performs default value verification across all per-pin and group registers.

For each of the per-pin control and group registers (GP0_GPIO_8 through GP0_GPIO_39; GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1; GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1; GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1; GP0_INTR2_INTR_EN1; GP0_INTR2_INTR_STS1; GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..4; GPIO_DOUT_GROUP1..4; GPIO_DIN_GROUP1..4): if a register is marked to skip for reset checking, it is not read.
If a register’s read mask is zero, its default value is not read and it is skipped.
Otherwise, read the register value and mask off bit 0 before comparison.
Compare the masked read value against the pre-defined default value for that location and record a default-mismatch if it differs.
Next, perform masked write/read checks using six data patterns in sequence for all registers.
For each data pattern, iterate over the same register list; if a register is marked as skipped for write, it is not written.
If the write mask for a register is zero, skip writing.
Otherwise, write the data pattern masked by the register’s write mask to the register.
After writes for the current pattern, iterate again to read back: skip if the register is marked skipped for write or has zero write or read mask.
Read back the register value and apply the read mask.

Compute the expected value by combining written bits (masked by both write and read masks) with the preserved default bits (masked by the inverse of the write mask and the read mask), then compare read vs expected.
If any comparison fails, record a write/read mismatch.
Completion: if any default mismatches or write/read mismatches were recorded, the test reports failure; otherwise, it reports success.

test_cases.Test Description: Configures per-pin input mode and falling-edge interrupts, iterates over GPIO 8–39 to generate individual falling edges, and verifies per-pin raw, grouped status, and clear behavior via ISR handling and bounded waits.
test_cases.Remarks: Timeout for interrupt wait is bounded and may be adjusted to the simulation time base. Pre-clears raw group status before enabling a single bit to avoid stale latches.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: test starts by enabling platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance and enabling the upstream system interrupt output.
Drive the external pad driver to a known high level using the memory-mapped output control at the specified address.

Initialization loop for 32 pins (GPIO 8–39): for each per-pin control register, configure input mode, enable falling-edge interrupt, and clear per-pin raw status, applying a small wait after each configuration.
Per-pin test loop (32 iterations): for the current pin index, compute a mask and pre-clear the group raw status corresponding to that pin.
Enable only the current pin in the group interrupt-enable register and apply a short wait.
Arm the interrupt wait flag prior to edge generation, then produce a falling edge by driving high followed by low at the memory-mapped output address.
Enter a bounded wait loop for ISR completion; decrement a timeout counter at each short delay. On timeout expiry, record an error for the corresponding pin.
ISR: upon handling, clear the wait flag and restore the external pad driver to high.
ISR: read the per-pin control to confirm the input level is low after a falling edge; record an error if not.
ISR: read the masked group interrupt status and confirm the bit for the current pin is asserted; record an error if missing.
ISR: clear the per-pin raw status using the per-pin control register and clear the group raw status register for the corresponding bit.
ISR: verify that the masked group interrupt status becomes zero after clears; record an error if not.
ISR: clear the upstream system raw status for the selected GPIO instance and clear the platform interrupt.
Completion: report pass if no errors were recorded; else report failure.

test_cases.Test Description: Enables rising-edge interrupts on GPIO 8–39, configures input mode via group IO control, generates a rising edge per pin, and validates grouped masked status, raw clears, and system status handling through an ISR with bounded waits.
test_cases.Remarks: ISR masks and then re-enables the group interrupt enable during service to avoid re-entrancy. Bounded wait with timeout is used to prevent infinite hang.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: test starts by enabling platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance and enabling the upstream system interrupt output.
Initialization: for each per-pin control register (GPIO 8–39), enable rising-edge interrupt.
Configure input mode for all relevant pins via group IO control registers.
Enable the entire masked group interrupt-enable register.
Per-pin test loop: for each pin index, drive the pad low to set a known level, arm the wait flag, then drive the pad high to generate a rising edge.
Enter a bounded wait loop for ISR completion; if the flag is not cleared before timeout, record an error and stop further iterations.
Optionally restore the pad to low and insert a short wait before moving to the next pin.
ISR: compute the bit mask for the current index and clear the wait flag.
ISR: read the masked group interrupt status; report success if any bit is set, otherwise record an error.
ISR: temporarily mask group enable to avoid further events during service.
ISR: clear per-pin raw status by writing to each per-pin control register, insert a minimal delay, then verify the masked group status returns to zero; record an error if not.
ISR: clear the upstream system raw status for the selected GPIO instance and verify the status bit is cleared.
ISR: re-enable the group interrupt-enable register and clear the platform interrupt.
Completion: report pass if no errors were recorded; else report failure.
